messages:
anya (DevEx): Strange one — sampleapp reports duplicate session-start when the app rotates during an in-flight streaming request. Happens on Pixel devices Android 11-14.

anya (DevEx): Repro: start chunked /stream request from Activity, rotate screen mid-upload, Activity lifecycle cancels the call, our background retry logic (WorkManager retry or RetryInterceptor) fires and server sees two start events with same session-id.

anya (DevEx): minimal OkHttp config we ship in SDK:
```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(true)
  .pingInterval(20, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .callTimeout(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
  .build()
val retrofit = Retrofit.Builder().callFactory(client).build()
```

anya (DevEx): ex logs from server and device:
```
[14:22:10.010] CLIENT start session=session-77 POST /v1/stream chunked
[14:22:11.500] CLIENT lifecycle: Activity#onDestroy -> call.cancel()
[14:22:11.501] NETWORK: java.io.IOException: canceled
[14:22:12.102] BACKGROUND retry attempt=1 -> re-exec request
[14:22:12.103] CLIENT start session=session-77 POST /v1/stream chunked
```

rohit (Android): sounds like two things combined: (1) call.cancel() marks the call as canceled and any subsequent call.clone()/newCall() may still re-run the same request if we try to re-execute it naively, (2) Activity rotation + WorkManager retry means the caller path may be running in a different thread/context and our retry code doesn't check for one-shot bodies.

rohit (Android): are we using Call.clone() anywhere in the SDK retry path? clone() is the right approach if the original Request body is repeatable, but for streaming bodies it's not. If the body is streaming/unrepeatable, clone() will still attempt to re-use the same sink and fail in weird ways or succeed and duplicate.

anya (DevEx): yes our older RetryWorker used request.tag(PROBLEM) to stash a Request and then newCall(request).execute() — I think that is the culprit.

marc (Platform): long-term fix: server-side dedupe on session-id is ideal, but on the client we should: (a) classify endpoints as non-idempotent (streaming) and avoid automatic retries, (b) add a small rebuffering wrapper for short bodies (<= 64KB) so retries are safe, (c) provide an idempotency header that callers can surface if they want retries.

taylor (QA): for immediate regression prevention: add a sampleapp test that rotates the device while request is active and assert server seen exactly one start. I can script this via adb rotate and tcpdump asserts in CI.

anya (DevEx): quick client patch I'm thinking: change WorkManager retry serialization to store only metadata (endpoint, headers) and fail fast if body.isOneShot (i.e., streaming). Pseudocode: 
```kotlin
if (request.body?.contentLength() == -1L || request.header("Transfer-Encoding") == "chunked") {
  // mark non-retryable
  throw RetryNotAllowedException()
}
```
Note: contentLength() may be -1 for streaming bodies.

rohit (Android): also recommend exposing a helper in the SDK: Request.Builder().addHeader("X-Client-Idempotency", "<uuid>") so app owners can opt-in to server dedupe while we design the canonical idempotency header.

deploy-bot: Created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/1792 - "Activity rotation + retry path duplicates streaming start; classify streaming endpoints as non-retryable"

anya (DevEx): i'll open a small PR with the WorkManager guard + sampleapp rotation test. We'll also add a short note to the Android troubleshooting doc: "Do not enable automatic retries for chunked/streaming endpoints; prefer idempotency tokens or server dedupe."

marc (Platform): thanks. follow-up: schedule a short sync with API team to design the idempotency header and server dedupe behavior.

taylor (QA): I'll add the adb rotation CI job and include a tcpkill variant to simulate flaky networks too.

anya (DevEx): 👍 thanks everyone.
